title: Software product (SaaS)

fields.label: What the product does
fields.help: Who it is for, the problem, and what it pulls together or automates. Name the tools or sources it connects to if any.

fields.label: How work flows through it
fields.help: Optional: the stages or columns your users move things through (e.g. Today, This week, Waiting on, Done) and typical items.

fields.label: Integrations
fields.help: The tools you connect to, and for each what comes in and what goes back, if you know.

fields.label: Plans and pricing
fields.help: Each plan with its price per seat a month, seat limits, the yearly discount, and what is in it.

fields.label: Results you can stand behind
fields.help: Optional: time saved or other numbers from real customers or a beta, and where they come from.

fields.label: Questions buyers ask
fields.help: Trials, data and security, cancelling, migration, support.

fields.label: Sign-up
fields.help: Your app's address for workspaces (e.g. plait.app/), and whether there is a free plan or trial.

fields.label: Brand colour
fields.help: Optional: as a name or hex code.

writerNotes: The hero runs one week of the product: threads from five sources tangle, then pass through the product (the knot), come out sorted into four lanes as work cards, a few move to the last lane, and everything settles into the product's window. Adapt all of it to the product: sources are the five things it pulls work from (tools, inboxes, channels, forms) with a one- or two-character glyph each; lanes are its four columns, the last one meaning done; cards are 8-16 realistic items for the example team (4 at most per lane), each from a source (s 0-4) in a lane (l 0-3) with an owner's initials, and one to three not already done marked ships: true.

stages: six steps in order (the mess before, connecting, sorting, becoming work, getting done, the calm after), each with a short name, a caption in the product's voice and a clock time across one week (Mon 9:14 ... Fri 16:30). demo: an invented example team's name and the readouts before and after (open items, tool switches, hours a week given back); keep them plausible and consistent with the captions.

cost: the calculator's starting team size, hours lost per person a week, hourly cost, and save (the percent of lost time the product gives back). save and cost.note must come from the brief's results; if the brief has none, use a modest figure (30-50) and say in the note that it is an illustration, not a measured result.

integrations: kinds are the categories (2-8), items the tools from the brief, each with what comes in, what goes back and how it syncs (Two-way, live; One-way in, every 5 min...). Never list an integration the brief does not name. start.preset ticks up to six of them in the setup preview.

pricing.tiers: the brief's plans, smallest first, price per seat a month (0 for a free plan), seat limit (max; 0 on the last plan), two to six features and a button label each. pricing.yearlyOff is the yearly discount in percent (0 if none). faq: two to eight questions with answers from the brief.

hero.title and hero.titleEm are a short two-part headline (four lines at most on a desktop). theme.accent is the product's colour, dark enough for white button text; theme.wordmarkFit is always "fit".
business.name is set to exactly the name in the brief and cannot be changed; brand.name is how it appears in the nav, the product window and the footer (often the same).
